title: fanoutqa: Identify the architects of five historical landmarks: the Eiffel Tower, the Sydney Opera House, the Taj Mahal, the Empire State Building, and the Parthenon. (9079b63f36e57692)

chat_history.content: Identify the architects of five historical landmarks: the Eiffel Tower, the Sydney Opera House, the Taj Mahal, the Empire State Building, and the Parthenon.

content.content: The user wants the architects of five historical landmarks: Eiffel Tower, Sydney Opera House, Taj Mahal, Empire State Building, Parthenon. Need to list architects (designers). Provide names. Possibly also include chief architects or designers. Should answer directly. No need for external tool as knowledge is common. Provide concise list.

content:
Here are the principal architects (or chief designers) associated with each of the five landmarks:

| Landmark | Year Completed | Principal Architect(s) / Designer(s) |
|----------|----------------|---------------------------------------|
| **Eiffel Tower** | 1889 (World’s Fair) | **Gustave Eiffel** – chief engineer of the Eiffel Company; the overall design was developed by the engineering team of **Maurice Koechlin** and **Émile Nouguier**, with Eiffel’s firm executing the project. |
| **Sydney Opera House** | 1973 | **Jørn Utzon** (Danish architect) – winner of the 1957 international design competition; the project was later overseen and completed under the direction of **Jørn Utzon** and the Australian firm **Ove Næss & Partners** after a long and complex construction period. |
| **Taj Mahal** | 1653 | **Ustad Ahmad Lahauri** – chief architect and master mason who supervised the construction; the overall design is attributed to the Mughal court’s team of architects and artisans under Emperor Shah Jahan. |
| **Empire State Building** | 1931 | **Shreve, Lombard & Harmon** – the architectural firm (lead architects **William F. Lombard** and **Alfred E. Shreve**) that designed the skyscraper; the project’s construction was directed by **John R. Olin** (project manager) and structural engineer **Fazlur Rahman Khan** (later contributions). |
| **Parthenon** | c. 447–432 BC | **Ictinus** and **Callicrates** – the two chief architects (master builders) of the Classical Athenian project; the sculptural program was overseen by the sculptor **Phidias**. |

*Note:* Many of these monuments involved large teams of engineers, artisans, and craftsmen, but the individuals listed above are the ones most commonly credited as the principal architects or designers.*
